description: Outpost Down is an immersive 1-4 player browser-based Mars survival and return-flight game. Explore a life-sized base, manage power and life support, investigate regional science sites, and drive the Wayfarer rover. Work wit your friends to do the realistic space missions through the mission.
summary: We developed an educational game that helps kids learn about Mars’ environment through interactive learning and small tasks that the game provides, helping them get familiar with terms and how stuff on Mars actually happens (ex. Sandstorms, cleaning solar panels) to simulate what it would be like to do a man mission on Mars. When you’re coming back to Earth, we use real Apollo mission data–Apollo 13 rising CO2, Apollo 12’s electrical trouble during launch, and the Challenger STS-51F faulty readings and the early engine shutdown. It addresses the challenge by simulating a Mars crash landing and deserting in a very oversimplified way using small tasks children can do. The Earth landing also has small quizzes that reference the data as mentioned earlier with small quizzes in a trivia type of fashion, which is already proven to help engage kids. It matters because it helps children picture themselves doing aerospace work through simulations and an open-world map.
details: It’s an educational web based game for children where the player is on Mars, stranded with their crew–multiplayer connected by a 5 digit code–where they’re in an open-world Mars map where they work together to help rebuild their rocqket to fly back to Earth. Its benefits are that it helps children grow a passion for space exploration and space technology, so somewhere in the far future they can pursue a field in aerospace. We hope to achieve a fun, entertaining and educational experience with our game for children to help them have a fun way to actually have fun and learn at the same time. For the models and VFX, we used Blender to create them. We used React ,Nodejs, Websockets, vitest, playwright, render to host the game, three.js.
